address: Pijlsteeg 31 / Warmoesstraat 173, Amsterdam: Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky block (stone-and-brick hotel front, 1970s concrete arcade wing, Damstraat corner fronts)
notes: Pijlsteeg 31 (BAG, built 1994 as the latest rebuild) is the Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky block between Warmoesstraat, Damstraat and Pijlsteeg: 701 3DBAG wall surfaces round several courts, so only the four photographed street runs are drawn and every other wall stays blank brick (otherWalls).

walls[0] = panel 70 (NW, w06-307): the hotel front on Warmoesstraat: a granite ground and first floor with a row of three shop windows and the arched NH GRAND HOTEL KRASNAPOLSKY entrance in the right-hand bay flanked by two lanterns, iron-railed balconies over the ground floor, two brick storeys with stone surrounds and piers, a loggia-like attic of tall windows under a flat roof. Drawn as 5 storeys x 4 bays, stone on storeys 0-1, a portal entrance, bar balconies on storey 1, cornice. Simplified: the two entrance lanterns (the lantern component floats 10 cm off this panel's wall and fails parts-attached); the carved stone cartouches and the string of stone caps between the brick piers; the attic loggia (one window per bay); the entrance lettering.

walls[1] = panel 121 (SW, w01-208): the 1970s concrete gallery wing on the Damstraat side: a shop arcade on slim piers, one storey of nine tall curved glass bays between brick-faced piers under a deep concrete fascia, and a blank attic band with eleven small vents. Drawn as ground glazed, one tall narrow-window storey in stone material and a blank attic storey. Simplified: the curved (barrel) glazing is flat, the stepped concrete corbels on the attic are not drawn.

walls[2] = panel 475 (SW, w05-212): the hotel front on the Damstraat corner, a cream-painted stone front with a three-bay glazed ground floor under an awning, a signed fascia (HOTEL) and tall blue-grey framed windows. walls[3] = panel 80 (SW, w07-208): the red-framed Asian Spirit shopfront with a tall mullioned shop window and iron-red upper glazing. Both are drawn as glazed ground plus wide-window storeys; the shop lettering, awnings and the HOTEL fascia sign are not modelled (shop signage is tenant-specific and was changed within the capture year).
Not photographed or not exposed: the courts, the Pijlsteeg side and the north-east wings (no panorama within 35 m or only over scaffolding); they stay blank.

Uninstalled 2026-10-14 (likeness triage, plan Part 1 lane D): the Krasnapolsky block's grey stone hotel front with carved bays, the cast-iron glazed winter-garden range and the ornamented cafe front were drawn as a red brick grid and cream boxes (every street group FAIL, dL up to 0.78) on a high-ride wall (277 of 2,000 sampled routes). Ornamented historic front: uninstalled; bespoke if it returns.
